AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guards G1, G2 and G5 per binding rule 4. The per-card transform is faithful in every detail that matters -- one upgrade level carried, enchantment carried when CanEnchant allows, deck-end placement, no RNG consumed -- but the candidate list wrongly includes Quest cards (G1), the batch is applied in selection order instead of deck order (G2), and the skippable 0-to-6 screen is modelled as always taking the maximum (G5).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): Quest cards are offered to Claws and are destroyed by it
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# builds the selection from `PileType.Deck.GetPile(player).Cards.Where(c => c.Type != CardType.Quest && c.IsTransformable)` (CardSelectCmd.cs:487) -- Quest cards are excluded by name. claws.py:25 passes `run.removable_cards()`, which is `[c for c in self.deck if not c.eternal]` (run.py:360-362). That matches C#'s IsTransformable for the deck pile exactly (IsTransformable reduces to IsRemovable == `!Keywords.Contains(Eternal)` for a card in a Deck pile, CardModel.cs:737-750), but it drops the Quest clause. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py batch3`): the ported QUEST cards are ['byrdonis_egg', 'lantern_key', 'spoils_map'], none of which is eternal, and driving the selector to pick one gives `byrdonis_egg still in the deck after Claws: False` where C# gives True. Both sides ported: Claws is granted by the ported Tanx shrine (events/tanx.py, confirmed by `batch3-pool`), and Byrdonis Egg is a real deck card with a real payoff -- its HATCH rest-site option is what grants relic/byrdpip, the sibling unit in this same batch. So the sim can silently eat a quest reward the game protects. Not merely a parity issue: a random card_selector (the default, run.py:390) will eventually pick it.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): C# removes every original first and then appends the replacements in DECK-INDEX order; the sim removes and appends one card at a time in SELECTION order
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardCmd.Transform(IEnumerable<CardTransformation>, rng) collects each original's pile and index, calls `item.Original.RemoveFromCurrentPile()` for all of them, then sorts the batch with PileIndexSort (CardCmd.cs:353-360, 405) before the append loop -- so on a Deck pile the new Mauls land at the end in ascending original-index order. claws.py:26-37 loops over `run.select_cards(...)` and calls run.transform_card per card, which removes and appends immediately, so the Mauls land in whatever order the selector returned (the default is `self.rng.sample`, run.py:390, which does not preserve candidate order). DORMANT: the Mauls are only distinguishable from each other when they carry different upgrade levels or different enchantments, so the divergence needs at least two picks that differ in one of those. It is not cosmetic when it happens -- deck ORDER feeds the combat-start shuffle, which run.transform_card's own docstring calls out as the reason deck-end placement was ported in the first place. Goes live for the conformance harness on any seed where Claws transforms two cards of different upgrade state.

guards.what: G5: `CardSelectorPrefs(prompt, 0, 6)` with Cancelable=false and RequireManualConfirmation=true (Claws.cs:24-28) -- MinSelect 0, so confirming with fewer than six (or zero) cards is legal
guards.rationale: The sim's `run.select_cards('transform_optional', candidates, 6)` takes min(6, len(candidates)) and, with the default random selector, always takes the maximum (run.py:384-390). The port's docstring names the skippable purpose, so the modelling is deliberate: the count is the screen's MAXIMUM and how many a player actually confirms is a policy decision the sim delegates to card_selector. Same family as relic/calling_bell's G3 in this batch -- a player-choice model, not an effect divergence. Flagged rather than waived because an installed selector that returns fewer than six is the only thing standing between this and a behavioural difference, and because MinSelect 0 means the game genuinely allows taking nothing at all.

guards.what: G3: `original.IsUpgraded && cardModel.IsUpgradable` -> one CardCmd.Upgrade (Claws.cs:36-46) vs `original.upgrade_level > 0 and maul.is_upgradable` -> one `maul.upgrade()` (claws.py:29-30)
guards.rationale: Two things checked here, both correct. (a) ONE level is carried, not all of them: C# tests IsUpgraded (level > 0) and upgrades once, and the sim does the same -- contrast audit/records/relic/archaic_tooth.json guard G1, where the sim carried every level and C# carried one. (b) The upgrade IS guarded by is_upgradable, so PROMPT.md bug class 14 does not fire -- Maul has max_upgrade_level 1 and this is the relic/bellows pattern, not the relic/astrolabe one. .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md sweep D does not list this site, and the guard is why.

guards.what: G4: the enchantment carry-over -- C# clones (`original.Enchantment.MutableClone()`) and enchants the Maul if `CanEnchant` (Claws.cs:47-62); the sim MOVES the original's enchantment and drops it if `can_enchant` fails (claws.py:31-36)
guards.rationale: Same observable. C# leaves the original's enchantment in place and gives the Maul a clone, the sim detaches and re-attaches the single instance -- but the original is transformed out of the deck in the same breath, so nothing can observe its enchantment afterwards. Both sides consult CanEnchant/can_enchant and both leave the Maul unenchanted when it fails. Distinguished deliberately from audit/records/relic/archaic_tooth.json guard G2, which is a gap because there the SIM invented a can_enchant condition C# does not apply; here C# applies it itself at Claws.cs:50. The amount carries too (C# passes enchantmentModel.Amount; the sim re-attaches the instance with its amount intact).

guards.what: G6: `CardCmd.Transform(transformations, base.Owner.PlayerRng.Transformations)` names an RNG stream (Claws.cs:30), and the sim's transform_card is called with no pick_rng
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md bug class 16's second half does NOT fire here, which is worth recording because the call site looks exactly like the relic/astrolabe N1 gap. Every CardTransformation Claws builds carries an explicit Replacement (the Maul), and CardTransformation.GetReplacement returns it without touching the Rng when Replacement is non-null (CardTransformation.cs:55-59). The sim's run.transform_card likewise only rolls when `into is None` (run.py:437). Zero draws on both sides, so the stream argument is inert. Rule 7: CardCmd.cs, CardTransformation.cs and run.py are not hashed here.
cards/maul.py is ported as CardType.ATTACK with max_upgrade_level 1, which is what G3's is_upgradable test depends on.

guards.what: N2: the `forPreview` pass -- C# runs CreateMaulFromOriginal TWICE per card, once with ModelDb.Card<Maul>().ToMutable() + UpgradeInternal + EnchantInternal for the selection screen's preview and once for real (Claws.cs:29, 33-46) -- plus CanonicalVars and ExtraHoverTips
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim. The preview pass is specifically confirmed inert for the model: it builds throwaway ModelDb clones and uses the *Internal variants, which bypass the commands and therefore the hooks, and it touches neither RunState nor any Rng.
